answer: Persistent Co-Signed Work Ledger. Each identity is bound to an endorsement chain co-signed by prior members, and standing is earned only through completed, mutually verified task logs. New members must contribute sustained labor—like maintaining a juniper monitoring post or repairing a jetty—before gaining voting weight. The ledger records continuous participation, so an attacker must operate many real agents across a karst landscape of scheduled duties for months, paying coordination and opportunity costs far above mass registration.
